opt2.name: The Shuttled Traverse
opt2.sub: Sisters → Oakridge, with the Wall driven

segs.name: Sisters → Camp Sherman
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Metolius headwaters on the Metolius-Windigo Trail. Store at Camp Sherman, mile 17 — the last resupply before the pass.

segs.name: Camp Sherman → Big Lake
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The Wagon Road's loose volcanic pumice, laid down by Belknap Crater. Riders call the surface "frustratingly unstable" and want 2.4"+ tires. Loaded and climbing, this is the grittiest hour of the trip.

segs.name: Big Lake → Clear Lake
segs.surface: Sand Mountain descent, then forest road
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Off the pass past Sand Mountain and down to Clear Lake.

segs.name: Clear Lake → Trail Bridge — the lava
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The hard part of the McKenzie River Trail and the only Advanced-rated riding on either option. Sahalie and Koosah falls, then Blue Pool. Riders call it fatiguing and occasionally unrideable — in either direction. Almost none of the difficulty is gradient; it is all rock.

segs.name: Trail Bridge → McKenzie Bridge — the flow
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: What the MRT is famous for: thirteen miles of fast, buffed singletrack beside the river. Bigelow and Belknap hot springs are both on it.

segs.name: McKenzie Bridge → FR-19 junction
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Paved. The original itinerary calls this leg King Castle / Olallie / O'Leary singletrack; the route file puts it on the highway, gaining 365 ft over 12 miles. Those trails top out above 5,000 ft.

segs.name: FR-19 junction → Cougar Hot Springs
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Still paved, still gentle. Soak at Terwilliger, then meet the van.

segs.name: THE WALL — driven, not ridden
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: 12.6 miles and 3,286 ft to the route's 5,018 ft high point — the climb the van exists to delete. Option 3 rides it; Option 5 never goes near it.

segs.name: Indian Ridge → Elk Camp
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The 23 miles that make Option 2 long. Technically moderate, but no water, no bail-out and no cell service the whole way.

segs.name: Elk Camp → Alpine Trail → Oakridge
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Sourgrass, then the Alpine Trail down to Westfir. The original itinerary gives this day as 14.2 mi / +1,633 ft; the route file makes it 18.0 mi / +2,244 ft.

opt5.name: The Oakridge Trail Finish
opt5.sub: Sisters → Oakridge, with the byway driven

segs.name: Sisters → Camp Sherman
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Metolius headwaters on the Metolius-Windigo Trail. Store at Camp Sherman, mile 17 — the last resupply before the pass.

segs.name: Camp Sherman → Big Lake
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The Wagon Road's loose volcanic pumice, laid down by Belknap Crater. Riders call the surface "frustratingly unstable" and want 2.4"+ tires. Loaded and climbing, this is the grittiest hour of the trip.

segs.name: Big Lake → Clear Lake
segs.surface: Sand Mountain descent, then forest road
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Off the pass past Sand Mountain and down to Clear Lake.

segs.name: Clear Lake → Trail Bridge — the lava
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The hard part of the McKenzie River Trail and the only Advanced-rated riding on either option. Sahalie and Koosah falls, then Blue Pool. Riders call it fatiguing and occasionally unrideable — in either direction. Almost none of the difficulty is gradient; it is all rock.

segs.name: Trail Bridge → McKenzie Bridge — the flow
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: What the MRT is famous for: thirteen miles of fast, buffed singletrack beside the river. Bigelow and Belknap hot springs are both on it.

segs.name: Transfer — the Aufderheide by van
segs.source: OpenStreetMap way geometry (NF-19)
segs.note: About 75 minutes to Alpine Trailhead #5. The whole connector problem, solved by declining to ride it. Option 4 spends two days on this road; Option 2 rides 23 miles of ridge above it.

segs.name: Alpine Trail
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The ride that put Oakridge on the map, rated 4.5/5 on MTB Project. Forgiving enough for a strong intermediate on an unloaded bike. Geometry taken from the same route file, which descends the Alpine on its last day.

segs.name: Larison Rock Road climb
segs.source: Estimated from trailhead elevations — not on the parent route
segs.note: Option 5's only real pavement, and a climb you could shuttle instead. 6.8 miles to 3,301 ft.

segs.name: Larison Rock descent
segs.source: OpenStreetMap geometry, USGS NED 10 m
segs.note: 3.0 miles, −2,014 ft, continuous. Trailforks rates it black diamond, MTB Project difficult. The hardest descending on either option.

opt7.name: The Flow Line
opt7.sub: Sisters → Oakridge, with the lava ridden around on the highway

segs.name: Sisters → Camp Sherman
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Metolius headwaters on the Metolius-Windigo Trail. Store at Camp Sherman, mile 17 — last resupply before the pass.

segs.name: Camp Sherman → Big Lake
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Loose volcanic pumice from Belknap Crater. Not technical in the rock sense, but deep sand on a loaded bike is where a less-experienced rider washes the front wheel. With the lava gone, this is the hardest handling of the trip.

segs.name: Big Lake → Clear Lake
segs.surface: Sand Mountain descent, then forest road
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Off the pass past Sand Mountain and down to Clear Lake.

segs.name: Lava bypass — RIDDEN on OR-126
segs.source: OpenStreetMap way geometry (OR-126)
segs.note: 8.6 paved miles from Clear Lake down to Trail Bridge, in place of the 11.8 miles of Advanced-rated lava. It is downhill the whole way and it is the single change that takes the hardest riding off the trip. The cost is real: Blue Pool and the Sahalie and Koosah falls all sit inside the stretch you skip.

segs.name: Trail Bridge → McKenzie Bridge — the flow
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The half of the McKenzie everyone comes for: thirteen miles of fast, buffed singletrack by the river, with Bigelow and Belknap hot springs on it. OR-126 parallels the whole thing if anyone wants out.

segs.name: McKenzie Bridge → Cougar Hot Springs
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: 12.5 paved miles, gentle. Combined with the bypass that is 21.1 miles of pavement on the whole trip. Soak at Terwilliger, then meet the van.

segs.name: THE WALL — driven, not ridden
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: The only driving in this plan: 12.6 miles and 3,286 ft to the route's 5,018 ft high point. Not technical — it is forest road — but it is a two-hour grind that would swallow the day. Everything else you ride.

segs.name: Indian Ridge → Elk Camp
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: 23 miles of moderate riding with no water, no bail-out and no cell service. Elk Camp is a dry camp — carry 12–16 L for four.

segs.name: Elk Camp → Alpine Trail → Oakridge
segs.source: Route file — Three Sisters Three Rivers GPX
segs.note: Sourgrass, then the Alpine down to Westfir and into town. Rated 4.5/5 and the Oakridge guides say that shuttled it suits "intermediate, expert, or even less experienced riders" — here you reach the top under your own power, but it is the same flowing old-growth descent, with trailheads #1–#5 as bail-outs.
